# Skelpr

> Surgical code retrieval for AI agents, PR reviews, and fixes. Skelpr finds the
> parts of a repository that matter, ranks them, and hands the agent a small,
> token-efficient context package with precise file:line citations. It retrieves
> and cites — the agent still does the reasoning.

Installation is public. Running requires a machine-bound lease obtained from the
activation service. Managed leases check in during use. Hosted embedding and
generation providers receive configured requests, and optional Langfuse tracing
can include source and outputs. MCP uses the host agent for reasoning.

## Docs

- [Install & activate](https://www.skelpr.com/docs): prerequisites, pip install on Linux/macOS/Windows, activation with your token, first run, troubleshooting, uninstall.
- [Home](https://www.skelpr.com/): problem, integration modes, benchmark evidence, requirements, waitlist.

## Evidence

- The historical Sock Shop report claimed 59% fewer tokens and 76% fewer file reads. Retained artifacts do not fully reconcile with the aggregate.
- The ten-task Django case study reported 37.27% fewer tokens across successive builds informed by those questions. Neither study establishes general or frozen-release performance.
- Standard setup uses Python 3.10+, Docker and a configured embedding endpoint. External PostgreSQL/Qdrant can replace Docker. Standalone generation requires a configured model provider. From 0.3.6, plain pip install skelpr includes CLI, MCP and local AST grammars.
